title: Protocol for Isolating Viable Human Central Nervous System T Cells
author: Engelenburg, Smolders, et al.
materials: This section outlines the preparation of essential buffers and stocks. For final concentrations and specific volumes, refer to the “materials and equipment” section.1.Preparation of 25% bovine serum albumin (BSA):a.Add 25 g of BSA to a flask and top up to 100 mL with Hanks’ Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS), no calcium, no magnesium, no phenol red.b.Dissolve at 4°C.Note: BSA dissolves slowly; prepare this solution well in advance. Do not stir or shake, as BSA foams easily, which can interfere with its performance in density gradient centrifugation. Instead, occasionally invert the container gently until the powder is fully dissolved.c.Filter through a 0.2 μm filter.Storage: Store at 4°C for up to 1 month.2.Preparation of washing buffer (complete HBSS, cHBSS):a.Prepare the washing buffer containing 0.5% BSA and 2mM EDTA according to the materials table.Storage: Store at 4°C for up to 1 month.3.Preparation of 10x Erythrocyte Lysis Buffer (ELB):a.Prepare a 10x ELB stock solution according to the materials table.b.Filter through a 0.2 μm filter.Storage: Store at 4°C for up to 1 year.c.Dilute to a 1x working solution using distilled water.Optional: Preparation of transcription and translation inhibitors.To mitigate ex vivo transcriptional changes, prepare stocks in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO):d.Actinomycin D: 5 mg/mL stock.e.Triptolide: 10 mM stock.f.Anisomycin: 10 mg/mL stock.Storage: Use 50 μL aliquots to avoid deleterious freeze-thaw cycles. Store inhibitors at −20°C for a maximum of one month.Warning: These inhibitors are acutely toxic. Handle them with extreme care by following PPE guidelines and by consulting the Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) before use.

steps.title: Prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Make all buffers and inhibitor stocks required for downstream cell isolation and handling.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 25 % BSA: add 25 g BSA to a flask, bring to 100 mL with HBSS (no Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, phenol red); dissolve at 4 °C by gently inverting until fully dissolved, filter through a 0.2 µm filter, store at 4 °C (up to 1 month).
Prepare washing buffer (cHBSS): make complete HBSS containing 0.5 % BSA and 2 mM EDTA (see materials table); store at 4 °C (up to 1 month).

Prepare 10× erythrocyte lysis buffer (ELB): prepare stock according to materials table, filter through a 0.2 µm filter, store at 4 °C (up to 1 year); dilute to 1× working solution with distilled water before use.

Optional transcription/translation inhibitors (store in DMSO):
  • Actinomycin D 5 mg/mL stock,
  • Triptolide 10 mM stock,
  • Anisomycin 10 mg/mL stock;
 aliquot 50 µL, store at –20 °C (max 1 month). Handle with PPE and consult MSDS.

steps.title: Set up workstation
steps.instruction: Prepare a sterile, temperature‑controlled environment and all required tools before tissue processing.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm a water bath to 37 °C.
Sterilize equipment (100 µm stainless‑steel mesh sieves, glass Pasteur pipettes, scissors, scalpels, tweezers) by dry‑heat at 160 °C for 2 h.
Clean the laminar‑flow hood thoroughly with 70 % ethanol.
Arrange a container of ice to keep tissue samples and cell suspensions at 4 °C throughout processing.
Optional: If cells will be cryopreserved, place a pre‑chilled freezing container (e.g., Mr. Frosty) filled with isopropanol in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Isolate CSF mononuclear cells
steps.instruction: Process cerebrospinal fluid to obtain viable mononuclear cells.

substeps.instruction: Pour CSF over a 70 µm cell strainer to remove debris.
Centrifuge the filtered CSF at 450 g for 10 min at 20 °C.
Lyse erythrocytes using the 1× ELB working solution (as prepared above).
Optional: Store the CSF supernatant at –70 °C for later protein analysis.

steps.title: Isolate peripheral blood mononuclear cells
steps.instruction: Recover mononuclear cells from post‑mortem peripheral blood using density gradient centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Mix Lymphoprep™ thoroughly by inverting the bottle several times.
Add Lymphoprep™ to a conical tube according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute the collected blood 1:1 with DPBS.
Layer the diluted blood gently on top of the Lymphoprep™ without mixing the two phases.
Centrifuge at 800 g for 30 min at 20 °C (acceleration 5, brake 0).
Discard the upper plasma layer without disturbing the plasma:Lymphoprep™ interface.
Collect the mononuclear cell layer at the plasma:Lymphoprep™ interface, avoiding the erythrocyte/granulocyte pellet.
Wash the recovered mononuclear cells once with cHBSS.
Lyse any remaining erythrocytes using the 1× ELB working solution.

description: The protocol described here facilitates the isolation of immune cells from rapid post-mortem, autopsy-acquired human central nervous system (CNS) tissues. Isolation is particularly challenging due to the high lipid content of the brain, the low frequency of immune populations, and the rapid degradation post-mortem. It outlines the steps for isolating T cells from multiple CNS compartments—including parenchyma (white and gray matter), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), leptomeninges, dura mater, and choroid plexus—as well as matched peripheral blood as established in our previous work.1,2,3,4,5 This protocol is optimized for T cell isolation and next-generation sequencing. Alternatively, this protocol can also be applied to isolate B cells or myeloid cells, such as macrophages and microglia, as described in earlier studies.6,7,8
